1. Why this lesson matters
A report can show a believable number while its DAX context, target grain, interaction or
validation is wrong. This lesson teaches one controlled reporting competency and how to prove
it.
2. What you are learning
Create explicit base measures for count, distinct count, revenue, cost, profit, margin and average
value; explain measures vs calculated columns.
3. What you already need / prerequisite
M05 Modeling pass. No DAX measure skill is assumed.
4. Picture it in your head
Fact rows -> explicit measures -> visuals. Reuse [Net Sales], [Profit] and other base measures
instead of recreating logic in every visual.
5. New words before we use them
Measure = named DAX calculation evaluated in context. Calculated column = stored row-by-row
result. SUMX = iterator that evaluates an expression per row then adds. DISTINCTCOUNT =
unique-value count. DIVIDE = safe ratio function.
6. Watch / visual source
RECOMMENDED_VISUAL. Chandoo - Learn 80% of DAX in an Hour | 3:00-15:08. Why use it: See
explicit measures, why measures beat auto calculations, and measure-vs-column before typing
the base measure set. Internal fallback: PBD1 learner book + DAX reference fully teach the base
measures.

PBD1 - Follow with me once
7. Follow with me once - fully worked teacher demonstration
Measures are model calculations evaluated when a visual/query asks for them. Calculated
columns are row-by-row stored values. Analyst KPIs should normally be explicit measures
because business logic stays named, reusable and testable. Use SUM for an existing additive
column, SUMX when an expression must be evaluated row by row, DISTINCTCOUNT for business
entities, COUNTROWS for rows, and DIVIDE for safe ratios. Teacher action: Create explicit
measures: Line Count, Order Count, Customer Count, Total Quantity, Gross Sales, Net Sales,
Total Cost, Profit, Margin %, Average Order Value. Save a card/table page and explain SUM vs
SUMX and DIVIDE.
8. What you should see / be able to say
Base measures reconcile to protected practice anchors; implicit raw-column aggregation is not
used as the final KPI logic.
9. Why it worked
The model is already trusted, the measure/report action answers a stated question under known
context, and a second calculation/filter/state check can verify the result. Visual polish is never
accepted as proof of numerical correctness.
10. Common beginner mistakes
Using implicit raw-column aggregations as final KPI logic; creating calculated columns for
measures that must respond to filters; using SUM when the business calculation is a row
expression; raw division with zero denominator.
11. If you get stuck - recovery ladder
If totals look wrong, check the source column, aggregation choice and whether the KPI needs
SUM or SUMX. If a ratio divides by zero, use DIVIDE rather than hiding the issue. 1) Restate the
business question and active grain/context. 2) Identify the exact
measure/visual/filter/relationship involved. 3) Reveal only a structural hint. 4) Open the protected
review only after saved evidence of an attempt. 5) Close review and solve a changed retry.
PBD1 - Do alone, validate and master
12. Now you do a small version alone
On a fresh scenario, rebuild the base measure set with different column names and prove one
measure using an independent manual/filtered check.
13. Validate your result
Base measures reconcile to protected practice anchors; implicit raw-column aggregation is not
used as the final KPI logic.

7. Follow with me once - fully worked teacher demonstration
Filter context is the set of filters active when a measure is evaluated: visual rows/columns,
slicers, page/report filters, relationship propagation and DAX filters. The measure formula can
stay identical while the result changes because the question/context changed. When a number
surprises you, ask: what filters are active and which relationships carry them to the fact table?
Teacher action: Create Category x Region matrix with Net Sales and Profit plus Region/Category
slicers. Predict three selections before clicking, test them, and write the observed contexts.
8. What you should see / be able to say
Matrix/slicer results match predictions or corrections; learner can name the active filters that
explain each change.
9. Why it worked
The model is already trusted, the measure/report action answers a stated question under known
context, and a second calculation/filter/state check can verify the result. Visual polish is never
accepted as proof of numerical correctness.
10. Common beginner mistakes
Thinking a measure has one fixed answer; forgetting page/report filters; using a slicer from a
disconnected/wrong dimension; blaming DAX before tracing relationship filter propagation.
11. If you get stuck - recovery ladder
If a number changes unexpectedly, remove slicers one at a time, inspect visual/page/report
filters, then trace relationship filter flow to the fact table. 1) Restate the business question and
active grain/context. 2) Identify the exact measure/visual/filter/relationship involved. 3) Reveal
only a structural hint. 4) Open the protected review only after saved evidence of an attempt. 5)
Close review and solve a changed retry.

PBD3 - Follow with me once
7. Follow with me once - fully worked teacher demonstration
CALCULATE evaluates a measure/expression under modified filter context. Start from trusted
base measures and change only the context needed for the question. REMOVEFILTERS is useful
when a denominator must ignore a breakdown filter. A common bug is leaving the denominator
filtered so every row appears to be 100%. Teacher action: Create East Sales, Electronics Sales,
All Category Sales and Category Share %. Validate category shares under a Region slicer and
explain the denominator context.
8. What you should see / be able to say
Share denominator behavior is correct; shares reconcile sensibly and do not all show 100%.
9. Why it worked
The model is already trusted, the measure/report action answers a stated question under known
context, and a second calculation/filter/state check can verify the result. Visual polish is never
accepted as proof of numerical correctness.
10. Common beginner mistakes
Removing too many filters in the denominator; each category share showing 100%; hard-coding
a filtered result instead of changing context; using CALCULATE to hide a relationship/model
problem.
11. If you get stuck - recovery ladder
If each share row shows 100%, inspect the denominator context and REMOVEFILTERS target. If
CALCULATE produces blank, check whether the filter value exists and whether a relationship can
propagate it. 1) Restate the business question and active grain/context. 2) Identify the exact
measure/visual/filter/relationship involved. 3) Reveal only a structural hint. 4) Open the protected
review only after saved evidence of an attempt. 5) Close review and solve a changed retry.

KPI measures and targets
Practice: matching PBD block in C1_M06_POWERBI_DAX_REPORTING_PRACTICE_GUIDE_RC1.pdf
1. Why this lesson matters
A report can show a believable number while its DAX context, target grain, interaction or
validation is wrong. This lesson teaches one controlled reporting competency and how to prove
it.
2. What you are learning
Build target/variance/attainment KPIs at the target table's real Region + Month grain and reject
unsupported daily target comparisons.
3. What you already need / prerequisite
Prerequisite: PBD3 plus the trusted M05 model. The new concept is introduced here before
independent use.
4. Picture it in your head
Actual fact (daily/line grain) + target fact-like table (Region + Month grain) -> compatible
monthly/region comparison.
5. New words before we use them
KPI = named business performance indicator. Target = planned benchmark. Variance = actual
minus target. Attainment = actual divided by target. Target grain = level at which the target is
genuinely defined.
6. Watch / visual source
BOOK_LED. Internal lesson - target grain and KPI contract. Why use it: The course-specific
Region/Month target grain is better taught against the exact supplied target table than through a
generic video. Internal fallback: PBD4 learner book + practice guide are the canonical route.
PBD4 - Follow with me once
7. Follow with me once - fully worked teacher demonstration
Targets are facts at a defined grain. If a target table is Region + Month, the model must compare
actual vs target at a compatible Region + Month grain unless the business supplies an allocation
rule. Variance = actual - target; attainment = actual / target. A polished card at the wrong grain
is still wrong. Teacher action: Relate Regions and Date to Monthly_Targets; create Sales Target,
Variance to Target and Target Attainment %. Compare by Region + Month and explain why daily
target is unsupported.

PBD5 - Follow with me once
7. Follow with me once - fully worked teacher demonstration
Time intelligence depends on a proper Date table: one row per date, coverage across the
required analysis period and an active relationship to the fact date. YTD, prior-year and
prior-month measures are context transformations, not hard-coded lookups. January is a key
validation period because previous month crosses a year boundary. Teacher action: Create Sales
YTD, Sales PY, YoY %, Previous Month Sales and MoM %. Build a monthly 2025-2026 line chart
and test January 2026 against December 2025 plus one prior-year period.
8. What you should see / be able to say
January 2026 previous month equals December 2025; prior-year measure uses the same
comparable period; YTD increases logically across months.
9. Why it worked
The model is already trusted, the measure/report action answers a stated question under known
context, and a second calculation/filter/state check can verify the result. Visual polish is never
accepted as proof of numerical correctness.
10. Common beginner mistakes
Using Month Name without chronological key; invalid/missing Date relationship; comparing
incomplete periods without saying so; January previous-month logic failing across year boundary;
raw division by blank/zero prior period.

Date relationship and the current date context before rewriting the measure. 1) Restate the
business question and active grain/context. 2) Identify the exact

review only after saved evidence of an attempt. 5) Close review and solve a changed retry.

7. Follow with me once - fully worked teacher demonstration
Visual choice is part of analysis. Cards communicate a few headline KPIs; line charts show
ordered time; bars compare/rank categories; matrices support detail; scatterplots show numeric
relationships. Page hierarchy should make the main question obvious before supporting detail.
Avoid decoration that carries no information and do not rely on color alone. Teacher action: Build
a 16:9 Executive Summary: 4-5 KPI cards, monthly trend, Category bar, Region bar and one
supporting matrix/table. Save a three-sentence design rationale.
8. What you should see / be able to say
Each visual answers a named question, formats are consistent, reading order is obvious and the
page does not rely on color alone.

The model is already trusted, the measure/report action answers a stated question under known
context, and a second calculation/filter/state check can verify the result. Visual polish is never
accepted as proof of numerical correctness.

color is the only meaning; different pages use inconsistent definitions.

keep 3-5 headline KPIs. If interpretation depends on color alone, add labels/signs. 1) Restate the

Measure
Dynamic calculation evaluated under context.
Calculated column
Stored row-by-row value; not a substitute for context-sensitive KPI measure.
SUMX
Evaluate row expression then sum.
DIVIDE
Safe ratio with denominator handling.
Filter context
Slicers/visual filters/page/report filters/relationships affecting evaluation.
CALCULATE
Evaluate under modified filter context.
REMOVEFILTERS
Broaden only the intended denominator/filter scope.
Target grain
Level where target is defined; do not invent finer-grain target.

Valid Date table + relationship + boundary validation.

Independent controls before trusting presentation.

Row security; not slicer/page hiding. Test with View As.
